title: Chapter 118 — Training Systems & Team Development
intro: The huddle, the drill culture, curriculum deployment, and the bench.

sections.title: The Daily Huddle
sections.content:
Every day, before doors open, gather the team for five minutes. Not fifteen. Not thirty. Five.

Wins: one minute. Focus: one minute — one priority for today. Product: one minute — one product fact. Numbers: one minute — where are we against goal? Energy: one minute — end with something that gets them up.

What kills a huddle: going over five minutes, airing problems in public, lecturing instead of energizing, skipping it because you are busy. The busiest days need it most.

sections.title: Drill Culture
sections.content:
Product knowledge drills. Objection handling drills. Demo practice. The team that drills together sells together.

Five minutes at the end of a team meeting: 'Quick drill — I am a customer who just said I can get it cheaper online. Who wants to take it?' The rep practices. The team watches. Everyone learns.

Rotate who leads. Ownership builds leaders. The veteran who teaches the greeting drill reinforces their own skills while developing the new hire.

sections.title: Building the Bench
sections.content:
Every great team has depth. If your top seller quits tomorrow, who fills the gap? If your trade specialist goes on leave, who handles the accounts?

Cross-train intentionally. Give retail reps exposure to trade. Give trade reps floor shifts. Develop your number two so they can step into any role on short notice.

The bench is not about replacing people. It is about resilience. A team with depth survives surprises. A team without depth is one resignation away from crisis.
